clauses.reason: Executive Order 11138, signed 1964-01-07 (29 FR 225), waives for Frederick Strauss the section 1 leave-of-absence limit and the section 3(a) reemployment-rights limit of Executive Order 9721, as amended by Executive Order 10103, and provides that he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence "for the period August 12, 1957, through September 16, 1962," for all rights and benefits under EO 9721, as amended. Its parents had been revoked in 1959 by EO 10804 section 2 except for employees serving with an international organization on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who did not elect coverage under it, and for vested rights; this order operates within that saved scope as the President framed it, and held evidence does not show whether Mr. Strauss elected coverage. Whether the waiver was used, and so exhausted, is not established by held evidence and is disclosed as open, not claimed. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table on page 12 of the held text prints this order as the one-line row "11138 Modifying provisions for the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations"; page 10 prints "10103 Amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations", and the number 9721 appears in the table on page 9. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11138 (29 FR 225, Federal Register of January 9, 1964), signed by Lyndon B. Johnson and dated January 7, 1964; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers every operative sentence; I confirm it. The order modifies Executive Order 9721 of May 10, 1946, as amended by Executive Order 10103 of February 1, 1950 (transfer of personnel to public international organizations): it waives, for one named person, Frederick Strauss, the section 1 limit on the period during which a transferred employee is considered on leave of absence and the section 3(a) limit on the time within which reemployment rights may be exercised, and provides that he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence from August 12, 1957 through September 16, 1962 for the purpose of all rights and benefits provided by EO 9721, as amended. Parent order: Executive Order 10804 of February 12, 1959 (24 FR 1147, held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10804.txt), section 2, revoked EO 9721 and EO 10103, except that "each shall be considered to" remain in effect for any employee subject to it who was serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and did not elect coverage under that Act, and for rights and benefits vested before that date. EO 11138 was issued after that revocation and modifies EO 9721 only for one employee whose deemed leave began on August 12, 1957, before the 1958 Act; the President thus treated EO 9721 as still applying to him within the saved scope. The held evidence does not show the enactment date of the Act (EO 10804 cites it as 72 Stat. 961) or whether Mr. Strauss elected coverage under it; if he had, the saved parent would not have applied to him and the waiver would have had no field of operation. That question bears on the waiver's effect, not on whether this order stayed on the books, and EO 10804, being earlier, cannot be an end of this 1964 order. EO 12553 revoked EO 9721, EO 10103 and this order on the same day. Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553 naming this order.

Whether the waiver was used, and so exhausted by performance, is not established by held evidence: no held source shows whether or when Mr. Strauss exercised reemployment rights or claimed benefits under it (owner ruling 2026-10-28: an unestablished event is not claimed as an interval). The 1959 revocation of the parent orders by EO 10804, with its saving for employees serving on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and for vested rights, came before this order and cannot end it; this order operated, as the President framed it, within that saved scope. The first end shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"The order's only command is the waiver and deeming rule for the named person; there is no independent continuing command. savings.reason: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception attached to its revocation list. The deemed leave of absence for August 12, 1957 through September 16, 1962 and any rights that vested in the named person under it before the revocation are accrued consequences, not a continuing command of this order.
